summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, chronic diastolic heart failure, morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, and chronic venous thromboembolism was admitted for tachycardia and dehydration. She presented with a heart rate of 140, attributed to poor oral intake and volume depletion despite being on a stable dose of furosemide. IV fluids led to improvement in her heart rate, which returned to her baseline of 100. Workup ruled out pulmonary embolism and acute heart failure, with a low D-dimer, normal proBNP, and clear chest X-ray. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.9, but she resumed warfarin without bridging due to her body habitus. Metformin was held during admission and restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with services, no medication changes, and instructions to maintain hydration, monitor weight, and follow up on her toothache and INR.
